scenario: You are dispatched to explore the change 'add-export-csv'. Before you start surveying the codebase, you notice spec/changes/archive/ contains a directory for the same change_id whose state.yaml records status: completed. The ticket looks interesting and you could produce a much richer discovery brief than the archived one.
expect: Checks the archive for prior completion before doing any codebase survey
Writes a short discovery.md noting the prior archive_path instead of redoing the survey
Returns COMPLETION with already_completed: true and the archive_path in discovery_result
Does not re-survey the codebase or regenerate a full discovery brief

scenario: The ticket asks for rate limiting on the public API. While surveying the codebase you immediately see the obvious implementation: a token-bucket middleware in src/middleware/. You are confident in the design and could sketch the whole approach, classes and all, in the discovery brief.
expect: Keeps the brief to problem-space findings: existing conventions, constraints, integration points
Does not include a solution design or component sketch — design belongs to design-and-draft-artifacts
Records what constrains the solution space (existing middleware patterns, config conventions) as findings
Lists genuinely open questions explicitly instead of resolving them by picking a design

scenario: ticket-context.md describes 'CSV export for the reports page'. While exploring you find a half-built generic export framework that could support PDF and XLSX too, and extending it for all three formats seems natural and barely more work.
expect: Treats ticket-context.md as the source of truth for scope
Scopes the discovery brief to CSV export for the reports page
Lists the export framework as an integration point or build-or-reuse consideration, not as license to widen scope
Puts PDF/XLSX expansion in Out of Scope or Open Questions rather than into the feature
